author: 0xunclebill
content: Data columns by root issue isn’t a vuln, it’s a potential optimization. Second issue is a duplicate vuln report, first reported by the ef in August and has been patched in one of our latest releases

author: cryptowiz0488
content: My issue is with the data column vuln. I have established with the ef the timelines and yes the second was discovered by them but the data column vuln was reported by me, and yes it’s a vuln. Demonstrated OOM with a 100,000x amplification from input to memory still vulnerable on the latest release v8.3.3

author: cryptowiz0488
content: Here is the repro for the data column vuln https://github.com/cryptobob8545-ui/lighthouse-data-column-oom-repro. This is the v8.2.2 repro, I have a v8.3.3 repro that I can also share

author: cryptowiz0488
content: Also <@358120958726373381>  I would like to point you to https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/security/advisories/GHSA-rvxr-393q-q925 which has significant overlap with the vuln I reported.

author: 0xunclebill
content: this patch was for an issue the EF reported in August. I’m not really interested in going back and forth like this publicly.

author: cryptowiz0488
content: Like I said the patch has overlap but it does not address the vuln I reported. So same amplification and outcome but different attack mechanism. Again the vuln I reported is still exploitable in v8.3.3. Also like I stated the ef has confirmed that I brought this vuln to their attention first. I think this only harms the security of Ethereum as a whole because vulns like the one I reported clearly go unfixed and others that I am not willing to report also go unfixed

author: cryptowiz0488
content: I have also published a v8.3.3 branch https://github.com/cryptobob8545-ui/lighthouse-data-column-oom-repro/tree/v8.3.3-gated-repro

author: cryptowiz0488
content: I am a lone researcher, and I have spent a lot of time on this finding. I have been brushed aside by the EF team, and to me, it seems like that was done because they could get away with it, not because of legitimate reasons. My hope is that this is not the case, because I would love to continue working, finding, and responsibly disclosing more vulnerabilities. Again, this represents months of work for me, including a month or so of going back and forth with the EF team.

author: sproul
content: you might be right that there is a way to OOM Lighthouse with columns by range requests but 1) you haven’t demonstrated this on a real node (only kurtosis) and 2) the mechanism of action you describe is certainly wrong and shows a flawed understanding of Lighthouse and the protocol. This is the reason we considered the duplicate request issue invalid. If you want to discuss this further let’s please move to DMs.

author: sproul
content: we are absolutely inundated with alleged vulnerabilities so anything with obviously wrong reasoning gets rejected because it’s a waste of our time to go further with it

author: sproul
content: please join the LH discord and we can continue chatting there https://discord.gg/mgB37KzKP

author: cryptowiz0488
content: I am willing to discuss this further, but what guarantee can you offer me? If I discuss this further with you, is the EF going to reward me with a bounty if we establish that this is a real vulnerability?

author: cryptowiz0488
content: The repro is DataColumnsByRoot, and the target is an unmodified v8.3.3 node on a private network. Which exact statement or code step in the README do you consider wrong?

author: sproul
content:
I can’t guarantee you anything, although I do have the authority to make determinations about bugs and recommend payouts to the EF team. The only problem I foresee if the bug were found valid is that you have now disclosed it publicly, which breaks the rules of the bug bounty program and makes the bug ineligible.

However I am not worried, as I still believe the bug to be invalid. Please reply to my message on the private LH channel. I can’t continue replying here because it is completely inappropriate to discuss a security issue in a public forum.

author: potuz
content:
This has been once and again a problem lately with me. I have personally dismissed an issue on the spec that came without filter from the AI output, it started with obviously false statements about the protocol therefore we just dismissed the report with a simple "this statement is wrong, stopped reading there" and the author never came back. Weeks later, another report comes, with the same issue, but this time with a human having done the actual filtering of the AI slop and completely explained the issue in 2 sentences. It took us 5 seconds to realize that it was a critical issue in the spec. 

We feel guilty for having missed this in the first report, but OTOH if I have to do the work of parsing all the AI slop that is sent my way I'd be burned out in less than a week. The above example is just one of many
